title: Specified native derived comparison intertwines localized Weil structure
statement: Let k₀ be a finite field and l a prime different from its characteristic. Let f:X→Y be a morphism of k₀-schemes, with compactification c, and let K be an object of the ordinary unbounded derived category of native Weil sheaves on X. Use the actual functors and comparisons of [def-sf-native-weil-induction-comparison-data]. Then Q_Y(beta_K) ≫ exchange_(U_X K) ≫ F(tau_X,K) = tau_Y,(FW K) ≫ beta_K, where tau is the localized structure isomorphism. No boundedness, constructibility or finite-type hypothesis on K is imposed.

source.place: First two paragraphs: the exchange followed by the image of the structure map defines the Weil structure. Native comparison proof step 6: normalization on a common K-injective model.

proof.text: For exact functors, expand the specified composition and natural-isomorphism comparisons. Their localization-factor identities give structure_fac and exactSquare_fac. For the right-derived Frobenius exchange, compose the defining derived-unit equations and cancel the exact Frobenius unit to obtain rightExchange_unit.

On a K-injective Weil complex J, precompose by Frobenius applied to the forgotten derived unit and postcompose by the ordinary image of the forgetful localization factor. Both are isomorphisms. Use the proper normalization, the exchange-unit equation, and naturality of the ordinary derived unit. The two sides reduce to the image of the termwise equation theta_(M J) = exchange_(U J) followed by L(theta_J), which holds by the definition of mapOfNatIso.

Package the two composites as natural transformations. Every derived Weil object is isomorphic to the localization of a K-injective complex, so naturality transports their equality from the preceding models to every derived object. Apply the same model calculation to the exact open extension, whose units are the inverse exact-localization factors, to obtain its structure equation.

Expand the specified compact-support comparison and exchange as their open/proper composites. Naturality of the proper exchange moves the open comparison through it. The open structure equation followed by the proper structure equation gives the required equality; the associators have identity components.

proof_origin.place: First two paragraphs; the specified comparisons and their derived-unit normalization, expanded by V4 into a termwise structure calculation and naturality on K-injective representatives.

from.place: Native comparison proof step 6: beta intertwines the localized structure with the native Frobenius exchange.

lean.statement:
theorem nativeWeil_comparison_structure
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k₀))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k₀))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k₀))] (c : Compactification f)
    (K : _root_.DerivedCategory (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X)) :
    (frobenius k₀ l Y).map ((comparison k₀ l f c).hom.app K) ≫
        (exchange k₀ l f c).hom.app ((forget k₀ l X).obj K) ≫
        (ordinaryImage k₀ l f c).map ((structureIso k₀ l X).hom.app K) =
      (structureIso k₀ l Y).hom.app
          ((ProEtaleWeilSheaf.rightDerivedLowerShriek k₀ l f c).obj K) ≫
        (comparison k₀ l f c).hom.app K

mathlib_searches.query: The canonical right derived comparison for a functor on fixed pairs commutes with the localized structure isomorphism and the Frobenius exchange

9 hits: NatTrans.naturality and generic cone and resolution component equations. Naturality alone does not assert compatibility of beta with structure.
